method.harness: _compute.py (PEP 723; uv run); Python 3.14.4 with compression.zstd, zlib, bz2, lzma, sqlite3 from the stdlib, and the pinned wheels brotli 1.2.0, lz4 4.4.5, cramjam 2.13.0; libbrotli 1.2.0 (system) via ctypes for dictionary brotli; git CLI
method.exactness: Sizes, ratios, counts and entropies are exact and deterministic for the pinned versions: generators are seeded, gzip headers carry mtime 0, git dates and identities are fixed and pack.threads is 1. Timings are medians of repeated single-threaded runs after a warm-up, on a 2-CPU cgroup shared with other tenants; they are reported as tiers, with cgroup throttling recorded before and after each timed phase.

zstd_then_compact.why: A zstd frame is one opaque stream: the keys, offsets and record boundaries that compaction reads exist only after decompression. 'Compacting the compressed log' therefore means decompressing all 39,366,976 bytes, compacting, and compressing again, which is compact-then-compress with an extra decode. Compression has no notion of a superseded record; it can only encode the whole history more cheaply. Systems that do both (Kafka batches, RocksDB blocks) compress small units the compactor can open one at a time.

entropy.method: order-k entropy is the empirical (plug-in) conditional entropy H(X_i | previous k bytes) in bits per byte, from overlapping (k+1)-gram counts of the file itself. It ignores the cost of describing the model, so order 1 and order 2 understate what a real coder could reach when samples per context are few: with 256 possible next bytes, an order-k estimate is only meaningful when orderk_samples_per_context is well above 256 (order 2 on the 1 MiB random input reads about 4 bits/byte for exactly this reason; the true value is 8). gzip_9 = gzip member at level 9 (mtime 0); zstd_19 = compression.zstd level 19; xz_9 = lzma preset 9 (xz container, CRC64); bzip2_9 = bz2 level 9. Achieved bits/byte include container overhead.
entropy.reading: achieved < order-0 means the compressor models context (repeats, previous bytes) that the order-0 histogram cannot see; entropy is relative to a model

counting_bound.statement: of all n-byte inputs, the fraction that can map to an output at least one byte shorter is at most (256^n - 1) / (255 * 256^n) < 1/255

lz_demo.parser:
Greedy LZ77: at each position take the longest match (>= min_match) that starts in the previous `window`
bytes, preferring the nearest on ties; matches may overlap the current position; else emit one literal. Window 32 KiB, minimum match 3, maximum 258 (DEFLATE's limits). This is not zlib's parse: zlib uses hash chains and lazy matching; raw_deflate_9_bytes is zlib's actual output for comparison.

corpus.repeat_distance_note: each version repeats about 98% of the previous one, one version-length (~3.63 MiB) back, so a window of 2^22 (4 MiB) is the first that can reach it
the same module in the next version sits one stdlib (~11 MB) later, so 2^24 (16 MiB) is the first window that reaches it

window.method: compression.zstd one-shot compress with options {compression_level: 3, window_log: w, enable_long_distance_matching: 2 (disable) or 1 (enable)}; every other parameter is the level's default as adjusted by libzstd (a window larger than the input is clamped to it, so window_log 26 and 27 coincide on both corpora, 45.6 MB and 33.7 MB); round trip checked at window_log 27 with and without LDM. level19_reference 'default parameters' leaves LDM on auto, which libzstd resolves to off here because the level-19 window is 2^23

wire.method: gzip via gzip.compress(mtime=0); br via the brotli 1.2.0 wheel (quality q, lgwin 22, generic mode); zstd via compression.zstd (window read back from the frame header: RFC 9659 requires <= 8 MB); dcz = RFC 9842 40-byte header (zstd skippable frame 0x184D2A5E, length 32, SHA-256 of the dictionary) + a zstd frame compressed with the dictionary as raw content; dcb = RFC 9842 36-byte header (ff 44 43 42 + SHA-256) + a brotli stream compressed with the dictionary attached as a raw LZ77 dictionary through libbrotlienc (the brotli wheel has no dictionary API). Every encoding was decoded and compared with the page. Byte counts include the dcz/dcb headers.
wire.note: rows: the dictionary is a different post from the same site (shared CSS, chrome and script), not an earlier version of the same page. delta_previous_version: the dictionary is the previous committed version of the same page on main's first-parent history (git show of the writings repo; for what-is-quirq, 107e64f is a merge whose first parent is a76229b), the case RFC 9842 is built for.

oracle.secret_note: synthetic: random.Random(2013), 32 hex characters; not a real credential
oracle.method: One synthetic HTML response (an inbox page) holds the secret in a link (?csrf_token=SECRET) and reflects attacker input in the text. The attacker's input is 'csrf_token=' + a 32-character guess whose first k characters are right and the rest are non-hex filler, so every guess has the same length. deflate_6 = raw DEFLATE at level 6 (what a gzip body holds; a gzip member adds a constant 18 bytes); brotli_5 = brotli quality 5; zstd_3 = zstd level 3. Masked: the token is sent as a fresh 16-byte mask plus (secret XOR mask) per response, the standard BREACH mitigation.

bombs.payload: 1,073,741,824 zero bytes, fed in 1,048,576-byte chunks (never held in memory)
bombs.method: Compression is streamed with each library's incremental compressor. 'bounded_call' is one decompression call asked for at most cap_bytes (zlib max_length, ZstdDecompressor/BZ2Decompressor/LZMADecompressor max_length, brotli Decompressor.process(output_buffer_limit)); zlib, zstd, bzip2 and xz return exactly the cap with the stream unfinished, so the caller can refuse; brotli's output_buffer_limit stops growing the buffer once it reaches the limit, so it can return more than the limit (overshoot_bytes). The full drain decodes in 1 MiB steps to prove the expansion. Times are single runs (tiers, shared machine).

rowid_check.table: notes(body TEXT) + index, no INTEGER PRIMARY KEY; 20,000 rows, 90% deleted (scattered)

sqlite.method: auto_vacuum set before CREATE TABLE; 100,000 rows inserted in one transaction; 90% deleted in one transaction either as the oldest 90% (ids 1..90,000, whole pages free up) or scattered (every row whose id is not a multiple of 10, so most pages keep a few rows); then VACUUM (NONE) or PRAGMA incremental_vacuum (INCREMENTAL); FULL truncates at commit. bytes_written_by_step is the process's /proc/self/io wchar delta (bytes passed to write(), including VACUUM's temporary database and rollback journal). deleted_rows_still_present_in_file_bytes counts deleted documents whose doc_id string can still be found in the raw database file, and where (this Ubuntu build compiles in SECURE_DELETE, so freed cells and freelist pages are zeroed).

one_shot.note: a full compaction reads the whole log once and writes only the live state

params.model:
A log-compaction simulation in the spirit of Kafka's cleaner: append-only segments of seg_bytes; the active
segment is never cleaned; when dirty/(clean+dirty) over closed segments reaches min_dirty_ratio, all closed
segments are rewritten keeping the latest record per key; a tombstone survives one cleaning (a stand-in for
delete.retention.ms) and is dropped at the next.

online_cleaner.reading: write_amplification = (bytes appended + bytes the cleaner rewrote) / bytes appended; space amplification = log bytes on disk / bytes of the live (latest-per-key, no tombstone) state

dct_demo.method: Synthetic 8x8 blocks (no image file). Level shift -128, the 2-D DCT of ITU-T T.81 A.3.3 (F(v,u) = 1/4 C(u) C(v) sum f(y,x) cos((2x+1)u pi/16) cos((2y+1)v pi/16)), quantization Sq = round(F/Q) with T.81 Annex K Table K.1 (luminance), which is the IJG 'quality 50' table unscaled, rounding half away from zero after snapping to 9 decimals (the smooth block's DC coefficient is exactly 56, and 56/16 = 3.5 is a tie that rounds to 4); reconstructed = dequantize, inverse DCT, +128, round, clamp. zigzag is the T.81 Figure A.6 order; rows are v (vertical frequency), columns u.

zstd_22_ldm_check.note: enable_long_distance_matching is a ZSTD_paramSwitch_e (0 auto, 1 on, 2 off). On auto, libzstd enables LDM when the strategy is btopt or stronger and the window is 2^27 or more, which is level 22 on this 211.9 MB input; the frontier's zstd_22 row therefore includes LDM, as lzbench's does.

timing_contention.note: codecs timed one at a time on one thread (about 1 CPU of the cgroup's 2-CPU quota); cgroup_cpu_used_s well above phase_wall_s, or a high throttled fraction, means other tenants shared the CPU

frontier.method: Ratios: each codec/level compresses the full Silesia corpus (12 files concatenated, 211,938,580 B) once, in two worker processes (not timed), and the output is decompressed and compared byte for byte. Speeds: the 12 MiB stratified sample (first 1 MiB of each file), one codec at a time in the main process on one thread, gc disabled while timing; warm-up = one compression of the first 256 KiB; compression median of 7 runs, or 3 when a run takes over 3 s; decompression median of 7 runs after one untimed verifying run. MB/s = sample bytes / median seconds / 10^6, 3 significant figures, reported with a tier because the machine is shared. ratio = original / compressed (the zstd and LZ4 README convention); pct_of_original = compressed / original * 100 (lzbench's convention). zstd_22_ldm_check is one extra untimed full-corpus job (level 22 with long-distance matching forced off) that shows what libzstd's automatic LDM contributes to the zstd_22 row.
